component.name: Oko
component.summary: Blocking detector: measures, does not bypass

description.p: Oko runs a series of network probes against services people actually use and says what stands in the way: a spoofed DNS answer, a middlebox that reads the server name, an address that is blocked, a Host header that is filtered, a connection cut at 16–20 KB.

ul.li: DNS: the system resolver against three DNS-over-HTTPS references
TLS with the real server name, and with a control name on the same address
Plain HTTP with the real Host header
Payload: where the body stops, at 16–20 KB or around 25 KB
QUIC: a 1200-byte Initial and the server's Version Negotiation
Direct against a SOCKS5 tunnel, so a block can be told from a slow server
24 targets in 11 categories, plus your own domains
English and Russian, dark and light themes, JSON and text reports
Updates itself, and checks the minisign signature before installing

description.p: Oko measures and explains. It does not bypass anything: no ClientHello fragmentation, no TCP tricks, no traffic of anyone else.

screenshot.caption: A run in the dark theme

description.p: Runs 24 targets in 11 categories, plus your own domains, and says what stands in the way: a spoofed DNS answer, a middlebox that reads the server name, a blocked address, a filtered Host header, a connection cut at 16–20 KB.
Compares a direct connection against a SOCKS5 tunnel, so a block can be told from a slow server.

Updates itself from GitHub releases and checks the minisign signature before installing anything. An update whose signature does not match is never installed, and a binary that lives in a system path is told to wait for the package manager instead of replacing itself.
English and Russian, dark and light themes, JSON and text reports.
